name: spar
paper_title: Shoulder physiotherapy exercise recognition: machine learning the inertial signals from a smartwatch
authors: David M. Burns, Nathan Leung, Michael Hardisty, Cari M. Whyne, Patrick Henry, Stewart McLachlin
license: Dataset: GPL-3.0 (github.com/dmbee/SPAR-dataset). Paper: IOP Publishing; the arXiv preprint 1802.01489 is what is stored here.
notes: 20 healthy adults (40 shoulders) performed 7 exercises from an evidence-based rotator-cuff physiotherapy protocol, 20 repetitions per shoulder, wearing an Apple Watch 2/3 on the exercising wrist. 6-axis IMU at 50 Hz; the released CSVs are ax,ay,az (g, gravity present) and wx,wy,wz (rad/s), with NO timestamp column, so the converter synthesises time at the documented fixed 50 Hz. CODE-VS-PAPER: 280 files = 20 subjects x 7 exercises x 2 sides, confirmed. VERIFIED AT CONVERT TIME: the quiescent (lowest-gyro-decile) |acc| across all 280 files is 1.026 g, confirming g-with-gravity; whole-file medians run 0.99-2.47 g because the exercises are vigorous, which is why the guard uses the quiescent decile. ENROLLMENT CAVEAT (measured, load-bearing): one file is a single continuous ~42 s bout of 20 repetitions, so repetitions are ~2.3 s apart and are NOT independent sessions; SPAR supports no same-subject enrollment curve (ceiling k=0). See docs/data/DATASET_EXPANSION_2026-08.md section 9. LABEL WORDING: the paper's Methods abbreviates exercises 5 and 6 as 'trapezius extension (TRAP)' and 'upright row (ROW)', while the release's own README.rst is more specific -- '5. Lower trapezius row with resistance band (TRAP)' and '6. Bent over row with 3 lb dumbell (ROW)'. The converter uses the README wording, which matches the shipped files and names the equipment. README.rst also independently confirms 50 Hz, accelerometer in G and gyroscope in rad/s.
